In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present health services system is not only a failure but a failure of a very special kind, namely, it has failed to achieve the very limited goals that it had set for itself.
the rural health services in India are a failure.

the health services system in India has failed to meet even the basic requirements of the masses, that it has not been able to provide even the minimum level of services which the Bhore Committee had in 1943 described as "irreducible minimum" and that even this minimum has not been provided to the masses of the rural areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present health services system in India is in the throes of a crisis, and that the crisis is not of the kind that is usually attributed to it, but one that is of its own making.
we have a very long way to go before we can claim to be in the process of developing a health services system for the masses of the country.
the present health services system is not only grossly inadequate but is also working inefficiently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health services system has to be built on a sound understanding of the social and cultural foundations of health behaviour of the people and of the health services system itself.
the rural health services are a part of the rural development process and that they cannot be developed in isolation from the development of the rural community as a whole.
there is a need to reorient the system to meet the real needs of the people and to make the system responsive to the needs.
